Helion CR-3#

The Helion CR-3 is a smaller, more portable fusion reactor designed for applications where a full Tokamak installation is impractical: military forward bases, remote industrial sites, emergency power restoration, and mobile command centers. The Helion uses a field-reversed configuration — a simpler plasma confinement approach than the Tokamak's magnetic torus — that trades some efficiency for dramatically reduced size and weight. The entire reactor fits inside a standard shipping container and generates 15 megawatts of continuous power, enough for a small village or a large industrial facility.

The Helion's fuel cycle uses helium-3 and deuterium rather than the Tokamak's deuterium-tritium mix, producing fewer neutrons and less radioactive waste. Helium-3 is scarce on Earth but is mined from lunar regolith by Crucible Industries' off-world operations and shipped down via the orbital elevator system. The fuel supply chain gives Crucible significant influence over Ouroboros's Helion program — a leverage point that neither company publicly acknowledges but that shapes their business relationship.

Ouroboros deploys Helion reactors on a lease-only basis, maintaining the same control model as their Tokamak installations. A Helion lease costs 800 Φ per day plus fuel, making it expensive for sustained use but competitive for temporary or emergency applications. The reactors are designed for rapid deployment — a trained crew can have a Helion reactor operational within 6 hours of arrival, compared to the 18-month installation timeline for a Tokamak. Approximately 300 Helion reactors are deployed worldwide at any given time, with Ouroboros maintaining a strategic reserve of 50 units for emergency response contracts.

The dependency this creates is the same as the Tokamak model, but more acute: a community that has never had reliable power becomes dependent on Ouroboros faster and more completely than one transitioning from an existing grid. Helix BioSeal Mk.VII Hemorrhage Arrest System#

The BioSeal Mk.VII is an injectable hemostatic foam system delivered via a pressurized 12mL cartridge injector. Upon injection into a traumatic wound cavity, the compound — a proprietary blend of synthetic fibrin analogs, chitosan-derived biopolymers, and platelet-activating peptides — expands to 40x its liquid volume within 4 seconds, conforming to irregular wound geometries and generating immediate mechanical tamponade. The foam cross-links with endogenous clotting factors to form a semi-permanent plug rated for wounds up to 8cm diameter and arterial pressures up to 180mmHg. The Mk.VII iteration introduced a thermal-reactive dissolve trigger: medical personnel can apply a specific low-frequency ultrasound wand (sold separately as the BioSeal Dissolve Probe DS-3) to liquefy the plug cleanly within 90 seconds, preventing the surgical complications that plagued earlier permanent-foam competitors.

What distinguishes the Mk.VII from its predecessors is the integrated chromatic indicator system — the foam shifts from white to deep amber as it saturates, giving field medics a visual bleed-rate assessment without imaging equipment. A secondary chemical marker reacts to infection-indicating bacterial enzymes, turning the foam red as an early sepsis warning. This dual-indicator system was developed in partnership with Cinderblock AI's diagnostic pattern libraries and is now considered standard in GLMZ emergency medicine training.

The BioSeal Mk.VII is standard issue for GLMZ Tier 2+ citizens' emergency kits, corporate security teams, and licensed paramedical contractors. In the Underbelly and lower-tier zones, counterfeit 'BioSeal' cartridges — often containing inferior foam with no dissolve capability — are rampant on the gray market. These knockoffs, called 'Hardplugs' by street medics, have caused numerous surgical fatalities when hospital teams couldn't remove the plug without extensive tissue damage.

Helix Biosystems Accelerated Bone Grafting System#

A medical system that fabricates custom bone grafts from the patient's own cells in 24 hours and integrates them into the skeletal system through a minimally invasive procedure. The ABGS scans the injury site, 3D-prints a bone scaffold seeded with the patient's osteoblasts, and implants it through a small incision where it bonds with existing bone within two weeks. The technology has made fractures, bone loss, and skeletal augmentation foundation work routine procedures rather than months-long recovery processes.

Helix Biosystems Anti-Aging Skin Treatment#

A topical treatment containing engineered stem cells and growth factors that reverses visible skin aging — wrinkles, age spots, loss of elasticity, and sun damage — over a 30-day treatment cycle. The treatment stimulates the skin's natural regenerative processes at an accelerated rate, replacing damaged cells with fresh ones and rebuilding the collagen matrix to restore youthful appearance. Unlike cosmetic surgery, the AAST produces results that are biologically genuine — the treated skin is not stretched or filled, it is actually younger at the cellular level. The treatment must be repeated every 2-3 years to maintain results.

Helix Biosystems Chimeric Organism Design Framework#

A genetic engineering platform for designing organisms that combine genetic material from multiple species to create novel life forms with desired characteristics. The CODF uses AI-assisted genome design to identify compatible genetic sequences from different organisms and combine them into viable chimeric genomes. The resulting organisms exhibit traits from multiple parent species — plants with animal immune systems, insects with mammalian sensory capabilities, microorganisms with multicellular repair mechanisms. Helix uses the platform primarily for medical and agricultural applications, but the framework's flexibility enables the creation of organisms that have no natural analog.

Helix Biosystems CRISPR-Omega Gene Editing Suite#

The latest generation of targeted gene editing technology, capable of making precise modifications to living human cells in vivo — without extracting the cells first. CRISPR-Omega uses engineered viral delivery vehicles that target specific cell types and organs, carrying gene editing payloads that activate only in the intended tissue. A single injection can modify liver function, enhance muscle fiber composition, alter immune response patterns, or correct genetic defects across the affected organ within weeks. The technology enables genetic modification of living adults, not just embryos — rewriting the code of a person who is already built.

Helix Biosystems Engineered Symbiotic Organism Platform#

A bioengineering framework for designing organisms intended to live in symbiosis with a human host, providing biological capabilities that augmentation achieves through hardware.   • Biologically integrated capability extension
social impact ESOP has created a new category of augmentation that sidesteps the cultural and political conflicts surrounding cyberware. Symbiont upgrades are not visible, not detectable, and not associated with the identity politics of cybernetic augmentation. This invisibility has made them the preferred enhancement path for individuals who want capability improvement without the social stigma or surveillance exposure of cyberware. The technology has also created a new form of inequality — symbiont-augmented individuals appear unaugmented and receive the social benefits of presenting as 'natural' while possessing engineered advantages.

  • Helix's symbiont organisms have been discovered to communicate with each other between hosts through chemical signals — creating an invisible network of biological information exchange between augmented individuals who have no idea they are connected.

Helix Biosystems LymphoDrain CX-3 Automated Lymphatic Assist Sleeve#

The LymphoDrain CX-3 is a semi-rigid wearable sleeve — available in full-arm, full-leg, and torso-panel configurations — that uses a network of micro-pneumatic chambers and piezoelectric compression nodes to mechanically stimulate lymphatic drainage in patients with compromised lymphatic function. Originally designed for long-term augmentation patients whose lymphatic vessels were disrupted during implant installation, the CX-3 mimics the natural peristaltic rhythm of healthy lymphatic tissue at programmable intervals, preventing the edema and immune-suppression cascade that frequently follows major cybernetic integration surgery.

The sleeve's inner lining incorporates a bioelectric feedback layer sourced from Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's flexible conductor technology, allowing it to detect subcutaneous fluid accumulation in real time and adjust compression sequencing accordingly. A companion application running on any Saltmarsh-compatible personal device displays lymphatic flow metrics and flags early signs of infection or implant-site rejection. Higher-tier versions include a pharmaceutical delivery reservoir that can inject micro-doses of anti-inflammatory compounds directly into lymphatic vessels during compression cycles, eliminating the need for systemic medication.

In clinical settings, the CX-3 is prescribed as a mandatory recovery device following any Tier 1 or Tier 2 augmentation procedure involving thoracic or limb implants. In the streets, it has found a second life as a performance device — long-haul courier workers and manual laborers in Palladian construction sites use unauthorized units to manage chronic limb swelling from repetitive strain, and combat-augmented mercenaries wear them during downtime to accelerate recovery from trauma edema. The street nickname 'Milker' is considered derogatory by long-term medical users but has been enthusiastically adopted by the merc community.

Helix Biosystems MyoStrand CR-400 Synthetic Muscle Fiber Bundle#

The MyoStrand CR-400 is a modular synthetic muscle replacement system consisting of braided carbon-polymer actuation fibers embedded with piezoelectric contractile elements, designed to be surgically implanted alongside or in replacement of native muscle tissue. Each CR-400 bundle replicates the form factor of a standard human muscle fascicle and interfaces with existing motor nerve terminals via Helix's NeuroClamp junction collars, which are included in every installation kit. The system delivers approximately 4.2 times the contractile force of equivalent biological muscle mass while consuming roughly 60% of the metabolic energy, drawing supplemental power from a subcutaneous CascadeCell-compatible capacitor node. The CR-400 is notable for its tiered activation architecture — the fibers are organized into slow-twitch analog layers for sustained load-bearing and fast-twitch burst layers for explosive force output, with the ratio dynamically managed by an embedded microcontroller that reads nerve signal cadence. Unlike full-limb cybernetic replacement, MyoStrand installations preserve native skeletal and dermal structures, making them visually undetectable and avoiding the legal reclassification complications that come with registered prosthetic limbs under GLMZ's Augmentation Registry Act. Arcturus Defense Solutions licenses a hardened military variant for special operations units, while the civilian version flows through Helix's authorized surgical network and a substantial black-market channel.

Helix Biosystems NeuroSalve Cortical Repair Gel NR-2200#

NeuroSalve NR-2200 is a direct-application neuroprotective and axonal repair gel formulated for use in cortical trauma, neural implant interface degradation, and surgical access wound closure in neurosurgical procedures. The gel is composed of a hyaluronic acid hydrogel carrier loaded with Helix's proprietary NeuroMatrix peptide complex — a combination of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) analogs, laminin-mimetic peptides that guide axonal regrowth, and a proprietary molecule designated HX-22 that temporarily downregulates microglial inflammatory activation at the application site. When applied directly to exposed cortical tissue or neural implant interface zones, NR-2200 forms a sustained-release depot that delivers therapeutic concentrations of its active compounds for 21 days before full biodegradation. Independent studies have demonstrated a 67% reduction in peri-implant glial scarring — the primary cause of long-term neural implant signal degradation — when NR-2200 is applied at time of implant installation.

The NR-2200 formulation is delivered in single-use 3mL syringes with a blunt-tip cortical applicator. It is temperature-sensitive and requires cold-chain storage below 4°C, a logistical constraint that has significantly limited its availability in lower-tier zones where reliable cold storage infrastructure is inconsistent. Helix Biosystems has announced a room-temperature stable variant (designated NR-2200T) for over two years, but the product has not materialized — industry analysts suspect the company is deliberately delaying the stable formulation to protect cold-chain distribution contracts with Kelpline Logistics.

NeuroSalve NR-2200 has become the gold standard for high-end neural augmentation clinics, where it is applied routinely during cortical interface installations to extend implant functional lifespan. Patients who receive implants installed with NR-2200 typically see 40% longer intervals between interface maintenance procedures compared to those without — a clinically and economically significant difference. In the chop-shop augmentation market, counterfeit NR-2200 products filled with plain hyaluronic acid gel (with no active compounds) are widespread, sold at 15% of legitimate product cost.

Helix Biosystems OculaRegen CR-5 Corneal Reconstruction Film#

The OculaRegen CR-5 is a single-use bioengineered corneal reconstruction film developed by Helix Biosystems for treating traumatic corneal damage, chemical burns, and the increasingly common 'augmentation erosion' syndrome caused by poorly fitted optical implants degrading the host corneal tissue. The CR-5 consists of a 0.1mm amniotic membrane analog layered with corneal epithelial stem cell precursors and a dissolvable photopolymer scaffold that maintains precise curvature geometry during the initial 72-hour adhesion window. The film is applied directly to the debrided corneal surface under local anesthetic in a procedure taking under 15 minutes, requiring no sutures — the photopolymer scaffold bonds to residual stromal tissue via UV-activated adhesion chemistry and then slowly transfers structural load to the growing epithelium before fully dissolving over 3–5 days.

The CR-5's most significant technical advancement over predecessor products like the CR-3 and competing films from Novafold is its incorporation of a gradient refractive index layer within the photopolymer scaffold, allowing the film to simultaneously correct moderate refractive errors during the healing period. Patients with corneal damage frequently experience severe uncorrected vision during recovery; the CR-5 effectively serves as a therapeutic contact lens and regenerative scaffold simultaneously. The stem cell precursor layer is derived from a proprietary Helix Biosystems allogeneic cell line, meaning the product requires no donor matching and can be deployed from standard refrigerated storage with a 6-month shelf life.

In GLMZ's context of widespread optical augmentation, the CR-5 has become the standard of care for managing what the medical community calls 'implant aftermath' — the ocular surface damage left behind when optical augments are removed, fail, or are forcibly extracted. Ripperdocs performing unauthorized augment extractions rely heavily on CR-5 films obtained through gray-market channels, and Helix Biosystems has an active (if poorly enforced) diversion-monitoring program tracking serial numbers.

HoloPresence VP-12#

The HoloPresence VP-12 is Vantablack Media's flagship volumetric display system, capable of projecting full-color, three-dimensional holographic images into open air without any screen, surface, or viewing apparatus required. The system uses intersecting arrays of focused ultraviolet lasers to ionize atmospheric nitrogen at precise coordinates, creating points of visible plasma that can be modulated in color, brightness, and position at refresh rates sufficient to produce fluid motion. A single VP-12 installation can fill a volume of up to 200 cubic meters with holographic content visible from any angle in ambient lighting conditions.

Vantablack has deployed HoloPresence installations throughout GLMZ's upper tiers, replacing physical signage, architectural facades, and even windows with holographic projections that can be updated in real time. The Spire district is particularly saturated -- walking through the Spire means moving through a landscape where roughly 40% of what the eye perceives is holographic. Buildings appear to change shape. Advertisements materialize in mid-air. Corporate logos float above intersections. The boundary between physical and projected reality has become genuinely difficult to distinguish, which is precisely Vantablack's intent -- a population that cannot reliably distinguish real from projected is a population that can be shown anything.

The VP-12's military and security applications are substantial. Arcturus has licensed the technology for battlefield deception -- projecting phantom vehicles, false troop positions, and decoy structures that are visually indistinguishable from real assets at range. Corporate security firms use HoloPresence to create false corridors, illusory walls, and projected hazards that redirect intruders away from sensitive areas. The technology has also spawned a counterculture of 'holo-taggers' -- artists and activists who hack HoloPresence installations to project unauthorized content into corporate spaces, turning Vantablack's own infrastructure into a medium for dissent.

Independent Darknet Node Architecture#

The darknet is a parallel network infrastructure that exists alongside and beneath the corporate-controlled NeuralMesh and DataPike systems. It consists of independently operated nodes — servers, routers, and relay stations maintained by individuals and organizations who require communication channels that corponations cannot monitor, control, or shut down. Darknet nodes are physically located in basements, hidden rooms, abandoned infrastructure, and occasionally in plain sight disguised as other equipment. They communicate through a combination of methods: short-range directional radio links, laser point-to-point connections across building gaps, and parasitic signals hidden within NeuralMesh traffic.

The darknet's routing protocol, known as HydraRoute, is designed for resilience rather than speed. Data is encrypted in multiple layers — each relay node strips one layer of encryption to reveal the address of the next node, but no single node knows both the origin and destination of any message. The protocol fragments data into pieces that travel through different paths, reassembling at the destination. This makes interception difficult — capturing data at any single point in the network yields only encrypted fragments — but adds significant latency. A message that would cross GLMZ in milliseconds on the NeuralMesh takes seconds or minutes on the darknet.

The darknet serves a diverse user base united only by their need for corporate-invisible communication: political dissidents, criminal organizations, investigative journalists, privacy advocates, corporate whistleblowers, and intelligence operatives from both corponation and government backgrounds. The network has no central authority — nodes are operated independently, and the protocol is open-source, maintained by a pseudonymous developer collective. Joining the darknet requires an invitation from an existing operator and a physical visit to have your equipment configured — a security measure that ensures trust is personal rather than digital.

Independent Mesh Shield Cooperative Networks#

In districts where no corponation provides barrier protection and residents cannot afford commercial shield installations, communities have developed cooperative mesh shield networks built from salvaged, stolen, and jury-rigged barrier components. A mesh shield network consists of dozens or hundreds of low-power emitters — many of them components scavenged from damaged or decommissioned commercial systems — connected through improvised control networks and powered by whatever energy sources the community can aggregate: solar panels, micro-turbines, tapped power lines, and occasionally donated Ouroboros Energy credits.

The resulting barriers are weak by commercial standards — they might stop shrapnel, debris, and low-velocity projectiles but would fail against any concentrated weapons fire. They are also unstable, flickering and dropping as power fluctuates and individual emitters fail. Maintenance is constant and communal — mesh shield technicians are among the most valued members of any unprotected district, and their skills are traded and bartered like currency. The control software is typically open-source, written and maintained by volunteer programmers who share code across districts through darknet channels.

Despite their limitations, mesh shields represent something corponations find uncomfortable: barrier technology operating outside corporate control. Crucible Industries has repeatedly attempted to shut down mesh networks by claiming patent infringement on monopole emitter designs, but enforcement in unprotected districts is difficult when the enforcers would need to enter communities that view their shield as a survival necessity. Some mesh networks have evolved into sophisticated distributed systems that rival low-tier commercial installations, and the communities that maintain them have developed a fierce independence born from the knowledge that their protection is something they built themselves.

Independent Micro-Grid Power Cooperative#

Independent micro-grids are small-scale power generation and distribution networks operated by communities, organizations, or wealthy individuals who have chosen to disconnect from Ouroboros Energy's TrunkNet. A typical micro-grid combines multiple generation sources — rooftop solar panels, small wind turbines, methane digesters, salvaged fuel cells, and occasionally black-market Helion reactor components — into a local network that powers a building, a block, or a small district without any Ouroboros involvement.

The motivation for going off-grid varies. Some communities cannot afford Ouroboros's dynamic pricing and build micro-grids as an economic survival strategy. Others are organizations that require power supply independence for security reasons — a data haven, a black clinic, or a smuggling operation cannot afford to have its power controlled by a corponation that might be compelled to shut it off. A few wealthy individuals maintain micro-grids as a philosophical statement: rejecting corporate dependency on principle, even though connecting to the TrunkNet would be easier and often cheaper.

Ouroboros tolerates micro-grids with a studied indifference that many interpret as contempt. Their official position is that anyone who wants to generate their own power is welcome to do so, provided they don't tap Ouroboros infrastructure or sell power to Ouroboros customers. In practice, Ouroboros's circuit-level metering makes it trivially easy to detect when a building switches between TrunkNet and micro-grid power, and buildings that maintain both connections often find their TrunkNet rates increase after using micro-grid power — a practice Ouroboros attributes to 'demand variability pricing' and micro-grid operators attribute to punishment. The total micro-grid capacity in GLMZ is estimated at approximately 2% of total power consumption — enough to matter to the communities that depend on it, but not enough to threaten Ouroboros's dominance.

Iowan Behemoth Agricultural Platform#

The Iowan Behemoth is a fully autonomous agricultural platform manufactured by Ironclad Agrisystems. Standing 12 meters tall and weighing approximately 400 metric tons, each Behemoth is simultaneously a planter, harvester, soil processor, irrigation system, and territorial defense platform. The machine runs on a hybrid hydrogen fuel cell array and can operate continuously for 90 days between maintenance cycles. Its onboard AI — designated the Crop Optimization and Defense Intelligence (CODI) — manages all agricultural functions and security protocols without human oversight.

The Behemoth's dual role as farmer and killer is not a design flaw — it is the design. Ironclad's engineers determined that separating agricultural and security functions into different platforms created coverage gaps that raiders exploited. The Behemoth solution is elegant in its brutality: the same machine that plants the seed defends the crop. Anti-personnel systems include a rotating turret mounting chemical deterrent projectors, kinetic crowd-dispersal charges, and in newer models, a focused acoustic weapon capable of liquefying internal organs at 200 meters. The Behemoth does not issue warnings. Its threat assessment algorithm calculates crop value versus ammunition cost and acts accordingly.

There are 340 active Behemoths in the Iowa Exclusion Zone. They communicate via mesh network, share targeting data, and can coordinate pursuit patterns across hundreds of square kilometers. Raiders who have survived encounters describe them as terrifyingly fast for their size — capable of 60 km/h on flat terrain — and utterly silent until they choose not to be. The most unsettling aspect, according to survivors, is that the Behemoths continue farming around the bodies. The crop does not stop growing because someone died in it.

Ironclad Agrisystems Atmospheric Remediation Nanite Cloud#

The nanites have a programmed 90-day lifespan to prevent uncontrolled replication, requiring periodic redeployment.

Ironclad Agrisystems BioGas Reclaim XT-8 Anaerobic Digestion Cogeneration Module#

The BioGas Reclaim XT-8 is a self-contained anaerobic digestion and cogeneration unit designed for installation in food production facilities, vertical farm operations, waste processing nodes, and large residential collectives. Developed by Ironclad Agrisystems as a waste-stream closure solution for its VertiRoot VX-22 hydroponic column deployments, the XT-8 accepts organic feedstock — agricultural residue, food waste, human biosolids, and organic processing byproducts — into a sealed thermophilic digestion chamber maintained at 55–60°C by waste heat recapture from its own generation cycle. Methanogenic bacterial communities within the chamber break down feedstock over a 14–21 day retention period, producing a methane-rich biogas stream (65–72% CH₄) that is scrubbed, compressed, and fed to a Ringo Corponation-sourced 30 kW micro-CHP (combined heat and power) engine. The engine's electrical output powers the facility; exhaust heat is captured and recirculated to maintain digestion chamber temperature, and the liquid digestate byproduct is processed into a nutrient-dense fertilizer slurry usable directly in hydroponic or soil-based growing systems.

The XT-8's distinguishing engineering feature is its Adaptive Feedstock Algorithm (AFA), a Cinderblock AI inference module that continuously monitors biogas composition, digestion chamber pH, and feedstock input rates to optimize bacterial community health and gas yield. Earlier generation digesters required consistent feedstock composition to maintain output stability — a significant practical limitation in urban waste stream environments where input materials vary substantially day to day. The AFA dynamically adjusts retention time, temperature, and supplemental trace mineral dosing to maintain consistent output across highly variable feedstock mixes, achieving 85–92% of theoretical maximum gas yield under real-world urban conditions. The unit processes 400–600 kg of feedstock per day at rated capacity and occupies a 12m² footprint, making it viable for rooftop, basement, and sub-floor installation in urban environments.

The XT-8 is most commonly deployed in Ironclad Agrisystems' integrated urban farm complexes, where it closes the loop between food production waste and energy generation, dramatically improving the energy economics of vertical farming operations. It has also been adopted by several Tier 3 residential arcology cooperatives that aggregate building food waste streams to fuel community power generation — a model that has demonstrated 15–25% reductions in grid energy purchase costs for participating buildings.

Ironclad Agrisystems Desalination Membrane Technology#

An advanced reverse osmosis membrane that desalinates seawater at 95% energy efficiency — dramatically better than previous generation systems — using graphene-oxide membranes with precisely engineered nanopores. Ironclad deploys the technology in coastal desalination facilities that supplement GLMZ's freshwater supply, producing potable water from ocean sources at costs approaching freshwater extraction.

Ironclad Agrisystems Soil Remediation Microbiome#

An engineered microbial ecosystem designed to be introduced into contaminated soil, where it metabolizes heavy metals, petrochemicals, and industrial toxins, converting them into inert compounds over a 6-12 month treatment cycle. The system is self-sustaining once introduced and spreads naturally through groundwater connectivity.

Ironclad Agrisystems VertiRoot VX-22 Closed-Loop Hydroponic Column#

The VertiRoot VX-22 is a self-contained modular agricultural column measuring 4.2 meters tall and 0.9 meters in diameter, designed for dense urban installation in corridors, rooftops, abandoned infrastructure shafts, and repurposed parking structures throughout GLMZ. Each column houses sixteen stacked growth rings fed by a recirculating nutrient solution managed by an onboard Cinderblock AI microcontroller that adjusts pH, dissolved oxygen, light spectrum from embedded LED arrays, and harvest timing autonomously. A single VX-22 column produces approximately 180 kilograms of leafy greens, legumes, or tuber crops annually using 94% less water than conventional agriculture through closed-loop condensate recovery.

The VX-22's defining innovation is its mycelial integration layer — a secondary biological network of edible fungi inoculated into the column's growth medium that processes root waste, suppresses pathogen blooms, and produces a secondary mushroom harvest from the same footprint without additional inputs. Ironclad licenses proprietary fungal strains that are genetically tagged, meaning any unauthorized propagation of the mycelium outside the licensed column triggers a legal claim under GLMZ's Biological Asset Protection statutes. The columns connect to Ironclad's AgriNet data service via Saltmarsh Telecom uplinks, allowing remote diagnostics and automated nutrient cartridge delivery — also sold exclusively through Ironclad's supply chain.

Vertical column farms built from VX-22 arrays have become the primary food production infrastructure for Tier 2 and Tier 3 residential zones, as surface agriculture within GLMZ's footprint collapsed following the Lake Erie algal iron events of the 2070s. Corporate cafeterias at Tier 1 facilities use premium VX-22 Pro configurations. In the lower districts, community co-ops pool resources to maintain shared column clusters, though dependency on Ironclad's proprietary nutrient cartridges and licensed strains creates a structural vulnerability that corporate enforcers and supply-chain leverage disputes have exploited more than once.

Kelpline Logistics AquaReclaim DF-9 Greywater Cascade Purification Unit#

The AquaReclaim DF-9 is a building-integrated greywater recovery and purification unit designed for installation in the utility cores of mid-rise residential and commercial structures throughout GLMZ. The system intercepts wastewater from sinks, showers, laundry, and HVAC condensate lines before they reach the municipal sewer outflow, passing the water through a four-stage cascade: mechanical filtration, a bioreactor membrane seeded with engineered Helix Biosystems microbial consortia, UV-C sterilization, and a final electrochemical polishing cell that strips residual pharmaceutical compounds — a critical requirement given the high concentration of Lazarus Pharmaceuticals metabolites documented in GLMZ's water table since the 2070s. Purified output is certified for non-potable reuse including toilet flushing, irrigation of VertiRoot VX-22 columns, and industrial cleaning, reducing a building's municipal water draw by 55–70%.

The DF-9's bioreactor membrane is the system's most technically sophisticated and commercially controlled component — the microbial consortia are Helix Biosystems proprietary strains licensed to Kelpline under an exclusive supply agreement, and the membrane cassettes require replacement every 14–18 months at a cost that represents the majority of the system's ongoing operational expense. Kelpline's service subsidiary handles cassette replacement under mandatory maintenance contracts, with the used cassettes classified as biological waste requiring Kelpline-licensed disposal — a classification that conveniently prevents third-party analysis of what the membranes have filtered out of a building's water supply over their service life.

The DF-9 was initially positioned as a premium sustainability feature for Tier 2 corporate residential developments, but water pricing increases driven by GLMZ's ongoing freshwater management crisis have pushed the system's economics into viability for Tier 3 multi-unit buildings operating as cooperatives or under building management contracts. A significant grey market has emerged around refurbished membrane cassettes — technically illegal under the biological waste classification, but widely used in lower-district installations where the alternative is either unprocessed greywater reuse or full municipal water dependency at rates that consume 18–25% of a lower-tier household's monthly allocation budget.

  • A refurbished membrane cassette sold on the grey market contains microbial colonies that are not Helix Biosystems proprietary strains — they are something older, something that predates Kelpline's founding, and they are extraordinarily effective at breaking down a specific class of compounds
  • Kelpline's used cassette disposal facility has been accepting cassettes but not processing them — a warehouse in the port district contains fourteen years of biological waste from thousands of buildings, unsecured
  • A building's DF-9 unit has begun producing purified output that tests positive for a trace compound not present in the building's water inputs — something is being added by the bioreactor membrane, not removed
  • A Kelpline logistics driver has been quietly collecting water samples from DF-9 output lines across a specific district and delivering them to an address that doesn't appear in any corporate registry

Kelpline Logistics AquaSpine DS-3 Submersible Urban Transit Tube#

The AquaSpine DS-3 is a pressurized, submersible passenger transit tube system engineered by Kelpline Logistics to operate through the permanently flooded sublevel districts of GLMZ's lakeside foundations. Rather than fighting the water table that has reclaimed significant portions of the city's lower infrastructure, the DS-3 treats submersion as an operational condition, deploying articulated tube segments fabricated from Palladian-sourced pressure-composite panels that are anchored to submerged building foundations and lakebed bedrock. Passenger capsules — cylindrical, 14-seat units — are propelled through the tube network via electromagnetic linear induction drives powered by Ouroboros Energy tap nodes, achieving transit speeds of up to 120 km/h through completely submerged passages. The tube network maintains positive internal pressure slightly above ambient water pressure, preventing intrusion even in the event of minor seal degradation.

The DS-3 system incorporates a sophisticated leak-detection mesh embedded throughout its tube wall structure, a technology co-developed with Saltmarsh Telecom's sensor array division, that provides real-time structural integrity data to Cinderblock AI's network management system. When a segment's integrity score drops below threshold, the AI automatically reroutes capsule traffic and dispatches Kelpline's automated repair submersibles before human operators are even alerted. This level of autonomous infrastructure management has made the DS-3 network statistically the safest transit system in GLMZ by incident rate — a fact Kelpline advertises heavily while omitting that the network exclusively serves communities that no other transit operator considers commercially viable.

The AquaSpine network is the primary transit lifeline for approximately 340,000 residents of GLMZ's submerged lower districts, known collectively as the 'Sublevel Settlements.' Kelpline holds exclusive infrastructure rights to the flooded corridors through agreements with GLMZ's Port Authority, agreements that critics allege were negotiated when those corridors were first declared uninhabitable and their residents were still being evacuated.

Kelpline Logistics HarbourSkate MX-40 Magnetic Levitation Cargo Sled#

The HarbourSkate MX-40 is a fully autonomous, track-bound magnetic levitation cargo sled designed to operate within GLMZ's submerged and semi-flooded lower-tier dock infrastructure. Each unit rides a passive ferromagnetic rail embedded in waterproofed concrete channels, using onboard superconducting coils chilled by a closed-loop cryogenic nitrogen circuit to achieve frictionless glide at speeds up to 180 km/h in enclosed corridors. Payload capacity tops out at 4,200 kilograms per sled unit, and sleds can be chain-linked in automated convoy configurations of up to twelve units managed by a single Cinderblock AI routing node. The MX-40 distinguishes itself from competing cargo systems through its amphibious transition capability: when rail segments are flooded, the sled's hull shifts to a sealed buoyancy mode, activating a rear-mounted impeller to maintain cargo movement through partially submerged sections without requiring infrastructure shutdown or rerouting.

The system was developed in response to the chronic flooding of GLMZ's Port Sublevel districts, where traditional wheeled logistics broke down entirely during seasonal Great Lakes surge events. Kelpline integrated pressure-adaptive hull plating sourced from Palladian Construction composites and a redundant navigation stack from Cinderblock AI that allows the sled to make real-time rerouting decisions when sensors detect rail submersion depth exceeding safe maglev thresholds. Each sled broadcasts its status on the Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh frequencies, feeding logistics data back to Kelpline's central dispatch.

The MX-40 fleet is leased primarily to Tier 2 and Tier 3 licensed freight operators who cannot afford the aerial drone corridors maintained by higher-tier logistics providers. The sleds have become so embedded in lower-city supply chains that entire black-market economies have grown around hijacking or temporarily rerouting sled convoys, a practice known colloquially as 'rail ghosting.'

Kelpline Logistics TideRunner FR-12 Amphibious Surface Effect Shuttle#

The TideRunner FR-12 is a 24-passenger amphibious surface-effect vehicle produced by Kelpline Logistics for transit across GLMZ's extensive flooded districts, drainage canals, and partially submerged lakefront infrastructure zones. It operates on a captured air cushion that allows it to skim across water at approximately 85 km/h while also transitioning onto degraded road surfaces, flood ramps, and semi-submerged loading docks without requiring specialized infrastructure at either end of a route. The FR-12's hull is a composite of recycled high-density polyethylene panels over an aluminum space frame — utilitarian and cheap to repair with materials available in low-tier districts. Twin ducted fans at the stern provide thrust; a flexible rubber skirt system handles the surface transition between water and land with minimal slowdown.

Kelpline originally developed the FR-12 for cargo logistics in flooded outer-ring zones where conventional road vehicles are inoperable and the AquaSpine DS-3 submersible tubes are not installed. The design was subsequently licensed to several municipal transit authorities as a stopgap passenger solution, and an unlicensed gray-market variant — the 'FR-12 Ghost' — has proliferated in the outer canals with stripped navigation transponders and reinforced gunwales. The FR-12's lack of fixed infrastructure requirements makes it uniquely valuable in areas of active urban decay or deliberate flooding by drainage authority negligence. Its Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh-linked navigation array uses air quality differential data as a secondary positioning system when GPS spoofing is active in contested canal zones.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals CoagCascade DX-11 Disseminated Clotting Reversal Agent#

The CoagCascade DX-11 is a precision pharmacological agent delivered via pressurized auto-injector that rapidly reverses pathological clotting cascades — including those triggered by synthetic blood products like HemaForge RX-7 — without inducing systemic hemorrhage. The formulation uses tiered enzymatic inhibitors that deactivate fibrin cross-linking in a staged sequence, preventing the catastrophic rebound bleeding that plagued earlier anticoagulant interventions. Each injector contains a proprietary sensor-reactive compound that reads local thrombin concentration and modulates dosing in real time, making it effective across a wide range of clotting severity without requiring a calibrated medical professional.

The DX-11 was originally developed under contract for Meridian General Hospital's trauma wards, where augmentation-related coagulopathies had become a leading cause of post-operative death. The rise of black-market implant surgeries performed outside sterile environments created a second, larger market — street surgeons now stock the DX-11 as a standard kit item. Its auto-titrating mechanism means even an untrained operator can administer it safely in most cases, though overdose in patients with pre-existing vascular grafts remains a documented complication.

The injector housing is a matte gunmetal cylinder roughly the size of a thick marker, with a biometric safety ring that can be disabled by licensed clinicians or bypassed by anyone with moderate technical skill. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals sells the clinical-grade version exclusively through Tier 2+ licensed pharmacies, but a nearly identical grey-market formulation circulates in the Undersprawl under the name 'ClotBreak,' differing primarily in its lack of the concentration-sensing module — making dosing a calculated risk.

The flagship compound, CogniLift-7, enhances working memory capacity by approximately 300% for 4 hours, allowing users to hold and manipulate vastly more information simultaneously than the unenhanced human brain can manage.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals HemaForge RX-7 Synthetic Blood Suspension#

HemaForge RX-7 is a perfluorocarbon-hemoglobin hybrid suspension manufactured by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals that functions as a universal synthetic blood substitute capable of oxygen transport, clotting factor delivery, and immune modulation simultaneously. Unlike earlier-generation blood substitutes, the RX-7 formulation incorporates programmable nano-encapsulated clotting agents that activate via localized pH sensors, allowing the suspension to behave as normal plasma in undamaged vascular tissue while aggressively coagulating at wound sites. The suspension is shelf-stable for 18 months without refrigeration and compatible with all known human blood types, making it the logistical backbone of battlefield medicine, black-market trauma care, and corporate emergency response units throughout GLMZ.

What distinguishes the RX-7 from competitors is its secondary 'metabolic bridge' function — the suspension carries a proprietary micro-nutrient payload that sustains cellular viability in oxygen-deprived tissue for up to 40 minutes post-administration, buying critical time for surgical intervention. Helix Biosystems attempted to challenge Lazarus's patent on the pH-triggered encapsulation mechanism in 2181 and lost, cementing Lazarus's monopoly on this specific approach. The product comes in 500ml pressure-sealed ampules designed for single-handed field deployment, and in bulk 10-liter reservoir bags for clinical settings.

On the street, RX-7 is frequently diverted from Kelpline Logistics shipments destined for Tier 1 trauma centers and resold to unlicensed ripperdocs and underground combat arenas. Counterfeit versions lacking the genuine nano-encapsulation matrix circulate widely in Tier 4 and 5 districts, causing fatal clotting cascades when administered — a known problem Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has been accused of deliberately under-addressing to protect legitimate sales channels.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Longevity Monitoring Implant#

Lazarus pairs the implant with their Telomere Regeneration Therapy, using LMI data to optimize treatment timing and dosage.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Pain Management Neural Implant#

A neural interface application that gives the user conscious control over their pain perception — the ability to dial pain sensation from full intensity to zero on a mental slider. At intermediate settings, pain is attenuated to informational — you know you have been injured, but it does not hurt. The system includes an override that forces pain back to full intensity if life-threatening injury is detected, preventing users from ignoring fatal damage.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals SomnaGraft-9 Neural Sedation Patch#

The SomnaGraft-9 is a transdermal neuro-sedation patch measuring 4cm x 6cm, designed for use in procedural sedation, acute psychiatric crisis intervention, and pain management during field surgery. The patch employs a tri-layer delivery architecture: an outer hydrogel adhesive layer bonds to skin within 3 seconds regardless of moisture conditions; a middle microencapsulation layer holds a proprietary cocktail of GABA-potentiating compounds, synthetic endorphin analogs, and a Lazarus-patented molecule designated LP-9 (colloquially 'Lazarine'); and an inner iontophoretic layer uses a micro-battery to drive the compounds across the dermal barrier at a controlled, dose-regulated rate over a 6-hour window. LP-9 specifically targets the thalamo-cortical relay without suppressing brainstem autonomic function, producing deep sedation while preserving respiratory drive — a critical advance over earlier sedative patches that caused dangerous respiratory depression.

The SomnaGraft-9 incorporates a passive NFC chip that logs application time, estimated dose remaining, and skin conductance data to compatible medical devices. In licensed clinical settings, this data streams to patient management systems. The patch also features a tamper-evident color ring that turns grey if the patch has been removed and reapplied — a security measure introduced after widespread reports of patch harvesting, in which individuals would remove partially-used patches from sedated patients to extract residual LP-9 for recreational use.

Medically, the SomnaGraft-9 has become the preferred sedation method for augmentation surgeries performed outside licensed hospital settings — a booming market in GLMZ where unlicensed 'chop shops' perform neural implant work for lower-tier citizens who cannot afford licensed clinics. The patch's safety profile makes it attractive to operators who lack anesthesiologists, but the same accessibility has made it a primary vector for non-consensual sedation crimes.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Telomere Regeneration Therapy#

A gene therapy protocol that restores telomere length in human cells, effectively reversing cellular aging by resetting the biological clock of treated tissues. The therapy uses engineered retroviruses to deliver telomerase activation sequences to every cell in the body over a 6-month treatment course. Patients who complete the full protocol experience measurable biological age regression — a 60-year-old's cells test as a 30-year-old's. The treatment must be repeated every 10-15 years to maintain the effect, creating a recurring revenue model that has made Lazarus one of the wealthiest pharmaceutical entities in GLMZ.

Levitas HCP-8#

The Levitas HCP-8 is a flat-deck cargo platform measuring 40 meters by 20 meters that uses an array of 12 graviton emitters to cancel the gravitational mass of loads up to 500 metric tons. The platform hovers at a configurable altitude between 1 and 30 meters above ground level and is propelled by conventional electric ducted fans mounted at its corners. The Levitas eliminates the need for road infrastructure, bridge weight limits, and vertical clearance restrictions that constrain ground-based heavy transport — it simply floats over obstacles.

The platform's graviton emitters are arranged in a grid pattern beneath the deck surface, each independently controllable to maintain level flight even with asymmetric loads. The onboard flight control system continuously monitors load distribution and adjusts individual emitter output to prevent tilting or oscillation. Loading and unloading require the platform to descend to ground level and deactivate its emitters — the transition from floating to grounded state takes approximately 90 seconds and produces a localized gravitational distortion that makes nearby personnel feel temporarily heavier as the emitters spool down.

Crucible Industries operates a fleet of approximately 800 Levitas platforms worldwide, leased to logistics companies, construction firms, and military organizations. The platforms are not sold — Crucible maintains ownership and provides operators, maintenance, and the cryogenic consumables required to keep the emitters functional. A single platform lease runs 12,000 Φ per day plus fuel and cryogenic costs, making the Levitas economical only for loads that cannot be moved any other way. The platforms have become a common sight in GLMZ's industrial zones, drifting silently between warehouses and construction sites like rectangular clouds trailing frost from their cryogenic vents.

MagRail LTN-3#

The MagRail LTN-3 is the backbone of GLMZ's inter-tier mass transit system -- a magnetic levitation rail network that moves approximately 4 million passengers daily through a 740-kilometer web of elevated guideways connecting every tier of the city from the Spire to the upper Shelf. Trains levitate 12 centimeters above their guideways on superconducting magnetic fields, eliminating friction and enabling cruising speeds of 420 kilometers per hour on express routes. The system is silent, smooth, and fast enough that a commute from the Circuit to the Spire -- a distance that would take two hours by road -- is completed in eleven minutes.

Ringo designed the MagRail as both a transportation system and a social architecture. The network's routing, station placement, and fare structure are not neutral engineering decisions but deliberate mechanisms for controlling population movement between tiers. Express routes connect productive economic zones at high speed. Local routes through residential areas are slower and less frequent. The Shelf's MagRail stations are concentrated at the district's upper boundary, forcing residents to travel significant distances on foot or by informal transport to reach them. Fares are tiered -- literally -- with cross-tier travel costing exponentially more than within-tier movement. A Shelf resident commuting to a Circuit workplace pays roughly 15% of a typical daily wage in MagRail fares. A Spire resident commuting downward pays a rounding error.

The MagRail's physical infrastructure doubles as a tier boundary enforcement mechanism. The elevated guideways create corridors of restricted access at tier transitions, with station checkpoints serving as de facto border crossings where identification is verified, movement is logged, and undesirable passengers can be denied boarding. Ringo maintains that the checkpoints are security features. Critics observe that the checkpoints are positioned exactly where they would be if the MagRail were designed as a population control system, and that the security screening process takes significantly longer for passengers traveling upward than downward.

Mass Driver Accelerator#

A 3-5 kilometer electromagnetic linear accelerator that launches pressurized transit pods to suborbital velocity (Mach 6-12) using sequential magnetic pulses through superconducting coils. The pod rides a magnetic sled with zero physical contact — no friction, no fuel, only electromagnetism. Passengers experience 3.2g for 8 seconds during acceleration. The technology replaced conventional air travel for intercontinental point-to-point transit. 847 accelerators are deployed worldwide as of 2200, with the largest hub being the GLMZ Apex Complex (4 tubes, 40,000 passengers/day).

MediaFlow CDN-5#

The MediaFlow CDN-5 is Vantablack Media's content delivery infrastructure — the system that distributes news, entertainment, advertising, and social media content to every BCI and display device in GLMZ. The CDN consists of thousands of edge servers distributed throughout the city, each caching and serving content to nearby devices with minimal latency. When a BCI user accesses any media content, the request is routed to the nearest MediaFlow edge server, which delivers the content from its local cache or retrieves it from Vantablack's central content repositories.

MediaFlow is more than a delivery system — it is a filtering system. Every piece of content that passes through the CDN is scanned by Vantablack's content classification AI, which categorizes material according to Vantablack's content policies and the content access contracts of the user's governing corponation. Content that violates these policies — material critical of specific corponations, information about labor organization, independent news that contradicts Vantablack's sanctioned narratives — is flagged for review, delayed, or silently removed from the delivery pipeline. The user receives no notification that content has been filtered; their feed simply doesn't include it.

The censorship capabilities are granular and context-sensitive. MediaFlow can filter different content for different users based on their BCI identity, tier, employment, and location. A user in a Ringo-governed block might receive different news than a user two blocks away in an Arcturus-governed block, with each feed tailored to avoid content that the governing corponation has flagged as undesirable. The result is not a single censored internet but millions of individually curated information environments, each shaped by corporate interests that the user may not be aware of. Vantablack's standard content contract costs 50 Φ per user per month — a fee that most governing corponations absorb as a cost of maintaining narrative control over their populations.

Mnemon TRM-5#

The Mnemon TRM-5 is a neural recording system that captures, stores, and enables playback of complete human experiential memory -- not just visual and auditory data, but the full sensory spectrum including proprioception, emotional state, and cognitive context. A memory recorded by the Mnemon is not a video; it is a complete experiential snapshot that, when played back through a compatible BCI, allows the viewer to experience the original event exactly as the recorder experienced it -- seeing through their eyes, feeling their emotions, thinking their thoughts. The system records continuously, storing approximately 90 days of experiential data on an implanted solid-state archive before older memories are overwritten unless manually preserved.

TESSERA markets the Mnemon as a professional tool -- investigators use it to create legally admissible experiential evidence, medical professionals record procedures for training, and corporate executives record meetings to ensure perfect recall. The official use cases are mundane. The actual use cases have created an entirely new economy. Memory trading -- the sale and distribution of recorded experiences -- has become one of GLMZ's fastest-growing gray markets. A recorded experience of a Tier 5 luxury vacation sells for thousands. A combat memory from an Arcturus operator provides an adrenaline experience no simulation can match. More intimately, recorded memories of deceased loved ones have become the most emotionally valuable commodity in the city -- the ability to experience a dead person's last birthday, their last conversation, their last moment of joy, exactly as they experienced it.

The Mnemon's darker applications involve memory manipulation. While the official system records without alteration, modified firmware can edit recorded memories before playback -- removing details, adding false elements, or blending multiple memories into fabricated experiences that feel completely authentic. This capability has made memory-based evidence legally controversial and personally devastating, as individuals can no longer trust their own recorded experiences. TESSERA's official position is that memory tampering is a criminal misuse of their technology. TESSERA's classified position, according to leaked internal documents, is that memory editing capability is a feature, not a bug.

NanoForge NAP-6#

The NanoForge NAP-6 is an industrial nanofabrication system that constructs physical objects by assembling them atom by atom from raw feedstock materials. The platform consists of a sealed fabrication chamber — ranging in size from a desktop unit to a room-sized industrial installation — containing billions of microscopic assembly arms controlled by a central AI that coordinates their movements to build complex structures from the molecular level up. The process is slow by conventional manufacturing standards — a desktop unit takes approximately 6 hours to fabricate a component the size of a human hand — but produces objects with material properties impossible to achieve through conventional manufacturing: perfect crystal structures, gradient material compositions, and integrated electronic circuits with no seams or joints.

The NAP-6 requires feedstock cartridges containing purified elemental materials — carbon, silicon, various metals, and other elements in monoatomic form. Crucible manufactures these cartridges at specialized refinement facilities and sells them through a subscription model: the fabrication platform is sold at a subsidized price, but the feedstock cartridges are proprietary, DRM-locked, and priced at margins that make printer ink look charitable. A kilogram of carbon feedstock costs 800 Φ, compared to 0.50 Φ for industrial-grade carbon on the open market — a markup of 1,600 times, justified by Crucible as the cost of monoatomic purification.

The technology has found its primary market in medical implant manufacturing (where material perfection is worth the cost), military component production (where performance justifies any expense), and luxury goods (where molecular-precision craftsmanship is its own selling point). Consumer-grade nanofabrication remains impractical due to feedstock costs, but the technology's trajectory suggests eventual mainstream adoption — a prospect that would reshape manufacturing, supply chains, and the very concept of physical goods if feedstock prices ever fall to commodity levels.

NeuralMesh NMP-6#

The NeuralMesh NMP-6 is the network protocol that enables Brain-Computer Interface devices to communicate with each other and with digital infrastructure. Unlike conventional wireless networking, which transmits data through radio frequency signals to base stations, NeuralMesh uses each BCI as both a client and a relay node, creating a mesh network where data hops between nearby BCIs on its way to its destination. Every BCI-equipped person is simultaneously a network user and a piece of network infrastructure.

The protocol operates in a dedicated frequency band allocated by the GLMZ Communications Authority, using ultra-wideband transmission at power levels low enough to be safe for continuous cranial proximity. Data throughput per hop is approximately 10 gigabits per second, with typical latency of 0.3 milliseconds per hop. In a dense urban environment where BCI-equipped individuals are rarely more than 5 meters apart, the mesh provides coverage that is effectively ubiquitous — there is no location in GLMZ where a BCI-equipped person is out of range of the network, because there is no location where there are no BCI-equipped people nearby.

Axiom Systems designed NeuralMesh as the default networking layer for their BCI hardware, and the protocol has become the de facto standard as Axiom's BCIs dominate the market. The protocol includes built-in encryption, identity verification, and traffic routing, but Axiom maintains administrative access to the routing layer — they can observe traffic patterns (though not content, due to encryption), prioritize or deprioritize specific data types, and in extreme cases, isolate individual BCIs from the mesh entirely. This administrative capability is documented in the BCI's terms of service, which approximately 0.01% of users have read.

NeuralWall NF-8#

The NeuralWall NF-8 is a software security suite running on Brain-Computer Interface hardware that protects the user's neural connection from unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and hostile signal injection. In an era where BCIs connect human brains directly to digital networks, the boundary between 'hacking a computer' and 'hacking a person' has dissolved, and neural firewall technology has become as essential as the BCI itself.

The NF-8 monitors all data entering and leaving the BCI through the NeuralMesh connection, using pattern recognition to identify potential threats: unauthorized connection attempts, data packets that contain known exploit signatures, and signals that attempt to interact with the BCI's neural interface layer — the components that directly stimulate the user's brain. The firewall can block incoming threats, quarantine suspicious data for analysis, and alert the user to attempted intrusions. Its most critical function is protecting the neural interface layer — an exploit that reaches this layer can potentially read the user's thoughts, inject false sensory experiences, or trigger involuntary motor commands.

Axiom provides the NF-8 as a standard component of their BCI package, but the default configuration is basic — adequate against known threats but vulnerable to zero-day exploits and sophisticated attacks. Premium NF-8 configurations with real-time threat intelligence feeds, behavioral analysis, and dedicated security monitoring cost between 200 and 2,000 Φ per month depending on the protection tier. The security disparity between basic and premium configurations is significant: basic NF-8 users are essentially running consumer-grade antivirus on a device connected to their brain, while premium users have corporate-grade security. The implication is clear — the wealthy are harder to hack, and the poor are soft targets for neural exploitation.

Novafold Pharmaceuticals GraftSkin TS-7 Bioprinted Dermal Replacement Sheet#

The GraftSkin TS-7 is a roll-format bioprinted dermal replacement product manufactured in standardized 20cm x 40cm sheets, each seeded with the patient's own keratinocytes and fibroblasts cultured from a small biopsy sample processed on-site using Novafold's proprietary rapid-culture bioreactor cartridge. Unlike earlier graft technologies that required weeks of laboratory preparation, the TS-7 system produces a viable, patient-matched dermal sheet in approximately 72 hours, dramatically reducing the rejection risk that plagued allograft procedures. The sheet itself is a tri-layer construct: an outer silicone temporary barrier, a mid-layer of cultured epidermis, and a dermal analog matrix seeded with vascular precursor cells that integrate with host tissue to restore blood supply within 10-14 days.

The TS-7 system is designed to treat large-area burns, traumatic degloving injuries, and — increasingly commonly in GLMZ — the surgical removal of unwanted subdermal implants or corporate identification tattoos. The rapid-culture bioreactor cartridge slots into a compact benchtop unit the size of a microwave oven, making the system deployable in field hospitals, corporate medical bays, and — with the grey-market cartridge adapters sold by unlicensed vendors — in back-alley clinics. Novafold maintains strict cartridge serialization to prevent off-label deployment, but counterfeit cartridges using generic culture media have proliferated throughout the Undersprawl.

Applications have expanded well beyond trauma medicine. Cosmetic modification clinics use TS-7 sheets to provide seamless coverage following subdermal implant revision, and identity-change fixers prize the system for its ability to alter fingerprint patterns and remove biometric skin markers. The corporate security community is acutely aware of this second use case, and Novafold faces ongoing legal pressure from Tessera Corponation and Arcturus Defense Solutions to add biometric watermarks to all cultured sheets — a proposal Novafold has publicly resisted while quietly lobbying against its implementation.

Novafold Pharmaceuticals ImmunoVeil TX-4 Rejection Suppression Protocol#

ImmunoVeil TX-4 is a sustained-release immunomodulation system designed specifically for recipients of cybernetic augmentation implants, biological grafts, and synthetic organ replacements. Unlike traditional broad immunosuppressants that leave patients globally vulnerable to infection, TX-4 employs a targeted tolerance induction approach: a loading-phase injection series over 72 hours presents the immune system with molecular 'passports' — engineered peptide sequences derived from the patient's own tissue samples combined with implant surface antigens — training regulatory T-cell populations to recognize implant materials as self. Maintenance is delivered via a monthly subcutaneous depot injection of Novafold's proprietary compound NF-TX4, which sustains the expanded regulatory T-cell population without suppressing the broader immune response. Clinical trials demonstrated a 94% reduction in chronic rejection response in augmented patients versus placebo controls.

The TX-4 protocol requires a mandatory pre-treatment tissue typing panel processed by Novafold's central laboratory, a 3-day inpatient or monitored outpatient loading phase, and lifetime monthly maintenance injections. This architecture is deliberate ��� Novafold has engineered a subscription dependency directly into the pharmacology. Discontinuation of NF-TX4 maintenance causes regulatory T-cell population collapse within 8-12 weeks, after which the patient's immune system mounts an aggressive rejection response against any installed augmentation. In patients with deeply integrated neural implants, this rejection cascade can cause severe neurological injury. The company frames discontinuation risk as a 'patient safety consideration'; critics frame it as corporate hostage-taking.

ImmunoVeil TX-4 is the market-dominant rejection suppression protocol in GLMZ, holding licensing agreements with 14 of the 17 largest augmentation clinic chains. Competing protocols exist but are locked out of major clinical channels through Novafold's exclusive supply agreements. A growing black-market ecosystem has emerged around TX-4 synthesis, as patients who lose corporate medical coverage — and thus lose subsidized access to monthly NF-TX4 injections — face the choice between paying Novafold's full retail price (approximately 40% of median monthly Tier 3 income) or risking augmentation rejection.

  • Novafold's central tissue-typing laboratory database has been breached — every patient who has ever undergone TX-4 loading protocol has their full immunological profile, augmentation inventory, and home address in the stolen data, and the buyer is unknown

Novafold Pharmaceuticals VascuPrint DP-3 Vascular Graft Bioprinter#

The VascuPrint DP-3 is a point-of-care bioprinting unit developed by Novafold Pharmaceuticals capable of fabricating patient-specific vascular grafts in under 90 minutes using a cartridge-based extrusion system loaded with the patient's own processed endothelial progenitor cells combined with a Novafold proprietary fibrin-collagen bioink. The device is roughly the size of a large microwave oven, designed for installation in surgical suites but ruggedized for forward medical stations and high-end private clinics. A blood sample is drawn, processed through the integrated centrifuge and cell-sorting module, combined with the bioink cartridge, and the resulting patient-matched graft is printed to specifications entered by the surgeon via touchscreen or neural interface link — diameter, length, branching geometry, and wall thickness are all customizable within the system's parametric template library.

The DP-3 addresses one of the persistent bottlenecks in vascular surgery: the shortage of suitable graft material. Synthetic grafts of earlier generations had poor long-term patency in small-diameter applications, and harvesting autologous saphenous vein caused its own morbidity. The DP-3's patient-derived endothelial layer dramatically reduces thrombogenicity and immune rejection risk compared to off-the-shelf synthetic alternatives, while the fibrin-collagen matrix degrades and is replaced by native extracellular matrix over 6–18 months. The system's cartridge consumables are Novafold-proprietary and carry DRM-enforced expiration dates, ensuring recurring revenue regardless of hardware amortization.

In GLMZ, the DP-3 has become a status symbol for private surgical facilities competing for Tier 1 and 2 clientele, and its presence or absence is a quick read on a clinic's capabilities and corporate affiliations. Novafold offers the hardware at subsidized rates to clinics that commit to exclusive bioink cartridge purchasing agreements, creating strong lock-in dynamics. Several Tier 3 hospitals have acquired DP-3 units through Kelpline-brokered leasing arrangements, though the cartridge cost remains a constant budget pressure.

OceanPurge MRS-3#

The OceanPurge MRS-3 is a fleet of autonomous marine vessels designed to extract microplastics, heavy metals, and persistent organic pollutants from ocean water. Each vessel is a catamaran-hull platform approximately 30 meters long, equipped with cascading filtration systems that process 500,000 liters of seawater per hour. The filtration stages progress from physical mesh collection of macro-debris through increasingly fine membrane filters to a final nanofiltration stage that captures particles down to 50 nanometers — small enough to remove dissolved chemical contaminants and microplastic fragments that conventional filtration misses.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals entered the marine restoration market through an unexpected path: their pharmaceutical research required ultra-pure water for drug synthesis, and the nanofiltration technology they developed for that purpose proved effective at ocean decontamination. The OceanPurge fleet of approximately 400 vessels operates continuously across the world's oceans, concentrating on shipping lanes, coastal industrial zones, and the remnants of the Pacific and Atlantic garbage patches that were partially remediated in the 2150s but continue to leach contaminants.

The extracted contaminants are stored in sealed tanks aboard each vessel and offloaded at processing facilities where recoverable materials — rare earth metals, platinum-group elements accumulated in ocean sediment — are extracted for sale. The remaining toxic waste is vitrified into glass blocks and stored in deep geological repositories. Lazarus reports that ocean microplastic concentrations have decreased by 70% since the OceanPurge program's inception in 2168, though independent researchers argue the actual figure is closer to 45% and that Lazarus's measurements conveniently sample from areas recently cleaned by their own vessels.

OrbitLink SCB-4#

The OrbitLink SCB-4 is a constellation of 4,000 low-Earth-orbit communication satellites that provides global network connectivity independent of ground-based infrastructure. The constellation operates in orbital shells between 500 and 1,200 kilometers altitude, with inter-satellite laser links creating a mesh network in space that routes data around the planet at the speed of light through vacuum — faster than ground-based fiber optic transmission through glass. For long-distance communication, OrbitLink is actually faster than the DataPike.

Each satellite weighs approximately 250 kilograms and carries phased-array antennas capable of simultaneously serving thousands of ground terminals. The satellites are manufactured by TESSERA's orbital fabrication facility and launched in batches of 60 using Crucible's orbital elevator system. The constellation is self-maintaining: satellites that fail or deorbit are automatically replaced from a reserve of 200 pre-positioned spares, and the routing mesh reconfigures around gaps in real time. The constellation's design lifetime is indefinite — individual satellites are replaced every 5 years, but the constellation itself is designed to operate continuously without interruption.

TESSERA sells OrbitLink access in two tiers: standard access at 500 Φ per month provides 1-gigabit connectivity from any location on Earth, while premium access at 5,000 Φ per month provides 100-gigabit connectivity with priority routing and guaranteed latency below 20 milliseconds. OrbitLink's primary market is organizations that need connectivity outside of urban areas where ground infrastructure exists — remote industrial sites, maritime operations, military deployments, and rural communities. In urban areas, OrbitLink serves as a redundant connection for organizations that cannot afford network downtime, providing an alternative path if the NeuralMesh or DataPike is disrupted.

Ouroboros Energy Ambient Thermal Harvesting Grid#

A distributed energy collection system that harvests waste thermal energy from urban infrastructure — building HVAC exhaust, vehicle engines, industrial processes, and even human body heat in crowded spaces — and converts it to electrical power through thermoelectric generator arrays embedded in structural surfaces. The ATHG turns GLMZ itself into a power source, with every warm surface contributing to the grid. The system produces modest power per square meter but scales with city density, making the most crowded, industrially active districts the most productive energy zones.

Ouroboros Energy Atmospheric Carbon Capture Network#

A network of industrial facilities that extract carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and convert it into useful materials — carbon fiber, graphene, diamond, and hydrocarbon fuels. The ACCN uses chemical sorbents to capture CO2 from ambient air and catalytic processes to transform it into solid carbon products. The system is energy-intensive but powered by Ouroboros's micro-fusion reactors, making it effectively carbon-negative. The captured carbon is used in manufacturing, creating a closed loop where atmospheric pollution becomes industrial feedstock.

Ouroboros Energy Atmospheric Water Extraction Network#

A distributed network of atmospheric condensation units that extract potable water from ambient air humidity, even in relatively dry conditions. Each unit uses thermoelectric cooling to chill surfaces below the dew point, collecting condensation that is filtered and mineralized for consumption. The network scales from building-mounted units producing hundreds of liters daily to district-scale installations that supplement conventional water infrastructure. Ouroboros deploys the system as a complement to their energy infrastructure, since the condensation units require significant power.

Ouroboros Energy CascadeCell Mk.IV Supercapacitor Array#

The CascadeCell Mk.IV is a modular supercapacitor array system designed for rapid energy storage and discharge in high-demand urban environments. Each unit consists of 144 graphene-aerogel capacitor cells arranged in a thermally-coupled hexagonal lattice, capable of absorbing and releasing up to 8.4 megajoules within a 0.3-second discharge window. The array charges from any compatible grid tap or renewable input and can reach 90% capacity in under four minutes, making it the backbone of surge-demand management across GLMZ's lower and mid-tier districts.

What distinguishes the Mk.IV from its predecessors is the integrated CinderBlock AI load-balancing microcontroller embedded in each rack unit, which negotiates real-time energy trades across adjacent arrays on the Ouroboros LocalGrid mesh protocol. This allows a building or installation running multiple CascadeCell units to function as a distributed energy node, selling surplus back to the grid during off-peak hours or hoarding capacity before anticipated demand spikes. The system is physically robust — encased in a Palladian-fabricated impact shell rated for seismic events up to 7.2 magnitude — and is commonly installed in basements, sub-floors, and reinforced utility corridors.

The Mk.IV is ubiquitous in Tiers 2 and 3 infrastructure, powering everything from mid-block residential towers to black-market fabrication dens. Its discharge speed makes it particularly attractive to operators who need instantaneous power: industrial door systems, electromagnetic barriers, and — less officially — rail-gun emplacements and high-wattage disruption rigs.
