Veilstrike TBP-4#

A portable, deployable barrier system that projects a flat-plane force wall from a tripod-mounted emitter. The Veilstrike TBP-4 creates a 3-meter-wide by 2-meter-tall barrier of densely packed electromagnetic flux that stops ballistic and energy weapon fire while allowing the operator to fire through it from the protected side using phase-synced ammunition. The barrier is visually opaque from the threat side — a shimmering wall of distorted light that obscures the positions of those behind it — but transparent from the operator side, functioning as both cover and concealment.

The TBP-4 deploys in under four seconds and runs for approximately 22 minutes on its integrated power cell. Multiple units can be networked to create longer barrier walls, with TESSERA's proprietary mesh protocol ensuring seamless field overlap between adjacent projectors. The system weighs 11 kilograms and is designed to be carried by a single operator in a backpack configuration, making it practical for tactical teams that need portable hard cover in environments where physical barricades are unavailable.

TESSERA developed the Veilstrike for law enforcement and corporate security applications, but the system has found enthusiastic adoption among mercenary companies and well-funded criminal organizations. The phase-synced ammunition requirement — rounds must be encoded with the barrier's frequency signature to pass through — creates a lucrative consumables market that TESSERA exploits aggressively. A case of phase-synced 7mm caseless runs approximately 800 Φ, compared to 45 Φ for standard ammunition of the same caliber.

Vespid Dynamics Biological Sensor Network#

A surveillance system using genetically engineered organisms — plants, insects, and microorganisms — as living sensor platforms. BSN organisms are designed to detect specific stimuli (chemical compounds, electromagnetic emissions, vibrations, biological agents) and respond with bioluminescent or chemical signals readable by Vespid's monitoring equipment. A district instrumented with BSN organisms has living walls that detect explosives, trees that sense electromagnetic emissions, and soil microbes that identify buried objects — all invisible to conventional counter-surveillance because they are, to every test, ordinary living things.

Vespid Dynamics Chemical Synthesis Micro-Reactor#

A compact chemical synthesis system the size of a briefcase that can produce small quantities of complex chemical compounds from basic precursor materials. The CSMR uses microfluidic reactor channels etched into silicon chips to perform multi-step chemical syntheses that normally require laboratory-scale equipment, producing milligram to gram quantities of target compounds in hours. The system is programmable — load a synthesis protocol and the appropriate precursors, and it produces the output compound automatically. Vespid designed it for field synthesis of drone maintenance chemicals, but its ability to produce any compound from a programmable recipe has obvious dual-use implications.

Vespid Dynamics Environmental Weaponization Framework#

Vespid's bio-weapons division uses EWF to produce a constantly evolving catalog of biological agents that are technically classified as 'organisms' rather than 'weapons,' exploiting a regulatory gap.

WeatherForge AEP-2#

The WeatherForge AEP-2 is a regional weather modification system that uses a network of ground-based and airborne emitters to control precipitation, wind patterns, and temperature within a coverage area of approximately 500 square kilometers. The system works by precisely seeding cloud formations with hygroscopic particles to induce or suppress rainfall, using directed microwave emitters to heat atmospheric layers and redirect wind currents, and deploying stratospheric aerosol mirrors to modulate solar radiation reaching the surface.

TESSERA operates WeatherForge installations on behalf of corporate clients who require specific weather conditions — agricultural corponations that need rain on schedule, logistics companies that need clear shipping lanes, real estate developers who want sunshine for their luxury districts. The system cannot prevent natural weather events, but it can modify their timing, intensity, and location within its coverage area. Rain that would have fallen on a corporate campus can be redirected to fall three kilometers away. Heat that would have made an outdoor event uncomfortable can be vented upward through atmospheric heating.

The redistribution of weather creates winners and losers. When rain is redirected away from a corporate campus, it falls somewhere else — often on communities that did not request, pay for, or consent to additional precipitation. When heat is vented from a luxury district, the surrounding areas become warmer. WeatherForge does not create or destroy weather — it moves it, and the places it gets moved to are inevitably those without the resources to purchase their own weather modification. A single WeatherForge installation costs approximately 800 million Φ to construct and 5 million Φ per year to operate, placing it in the domain of the wealthiest corponations and municipal authorities.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric CellStack BM-3 Biological Microbial Fuel Cell Implant#

The CellStack BM-3 is a surgically implanted biological microbial fuel cell array designed to harvest electrical energy from the electrochemical activity of engineered gut microbiome colonies. Developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric as a long-duration auxiliary power source for high-draw neural augmentations, the BM-3 consists of three titanium-encased fuel cell chambers implanted in the peritoneal space, each seeded with a proprietary strain of Zheng-Dao's GeoElectric-7 exoelectrogenic bacteria. These organisms oxidize metabolic byproducts — acetate, lactate, and short-chain fatty acids — drawn passively from intestinal interstitial fluid, generating a sustained low-amperage direct current output of 15–40 mA at 0.8–1.2 V per chamber. A tri-chamber array produces sufficient power to continuously supplement or replace standard battery packs for mid-tier neural implants, eliminating the need for external recharging in routine use.

The BM-3's key innovation over earlier biofuel cell prototypes is its Symbiotic Interface Layer (SIL) — a semi-permeable hydrogel membrane coating each chamber that allows metabolite exchange while preventing immune recognition of the bacterial colonies. This dramatically reduces the chronic inflammation and fibrous encapsulation that rendered previous designs clinically unreliable within months of implantation. Combined with Novafold's ImmunoVeil TX-4 rejection suppression protocol as a standard co-prescription, the BM-3 achieves a clinically validated operational lifespan of 6–9 years before bacterial colony viability declines and chamber replacement is required. Output degrades predictably with poor nutrition, illness, or significant metabolic disruption — a vulnerability with real-world consequences for users in food-insecure environments.

The BM-3 is primarily marketed to Tier 2 and Tier 3 augmented citizens who rely on high-draw cortical or sensory implants but lack the infrastructure access or financial means to maintain dedicated external charging hardware. In practice, it has also become popular among operatives and couriers in professions where going off-grid for extended periods is operationally necessary — the implant generates no detectable electromagnetic signature during normal operation, making it attractive for those who need to disappear from power-grid monitoring systems.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric FluxSpine BX-7 Kinetic Harvest Implant#

The FluxSpine BX-7 is a surgically-implanted piezoelectric energy harvesting system that extracts usable electrical power from the mechanical stress of the host's skeletal and muscular activity. A lattice of flexible piezoelectric film strips — approximately 0.3mm thick — is bonded to the periosteum of the spine, femurs, and tibiae during a four-hour implantation procedure. Each flex, step, and postural adjustment generates micro-currents that are rectified and stored in a subcutaneous lithium-ceramic buffer cell seated near the iliac crest. Under normal ambulatory conditions, the BX-7 generates between 18 and 34 milliwatts continuously — insufficient for power-hungry augmentations alone, but enough to meaningfully extend the operational life of neural interfaces, retinal overlays, and embedded comms gear.

Zheng-Dao's key innovation in the BX-7 over earlier kinetic harvest systems is the BioSync adaptive film calibration protocol, which uses the implant's onboard microprocessor to continuously remap which film segments are generating optimal yield based on the host's gait, posture, and activity patterns. Over approximately six weeks post-implantation, the system effectively personalizes itself to the individual, improving output by an average of 40% compared to factory defaults. The buffer cell charges conventional augmentation power sockets via a subcutaneous induction pad, eliminating the need for the host to consciously manage charging cycles.

The BX-7 is standard equipment for Tier 3 and Tier 4 citizens who carry augmentations but cannot reliably afford or access charging infrastructure. It's also heavily used in the courier, dockworker, and construction labor sectors, where high daily step counts translate to meaningful energy yields. A significant gray market exists for BX-7 units harvested from deceased donors, which carry the previous host's calibration data and require painful re-calibration procedures.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric NerveBridge SX-11 Peripheral Nerve Regeneration Conduit#

The NerveBridge SX-11 is a biodegradable electroactive conduit system developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric for repairing severed or severely damaged peripheral nerves in patients with traumatic limb injuries or augmentation-related nerve shear. The conduit itself is a 2–40cm tube constructed from a piezoelectric silk-fibroin matrix seeded with Schwann cell analogs — lab-grown support cells that guide regenerating axons across the gap site. A micro-embedded electrode array along the conduit's inner surface delivers pulsed low-frequency electrical stimulation autonomously, drawing power from the body's own bioelectric field through Zheng-Dao's proprietary ambient harvest circuitry, eliminating the need for external power sources or battery replacement.

The SX-11 represents the third major revision of Zheng-Dao's nerve conduit line, incorporating lessons from the SX-9's widely reported fibrotic encapsulation failures. The silk-fibroin matrix degrades cleanly over 8–12 months as the regenerating nerve matures, leaving no permanent foreign body. Critically, the SX-11 includes a wireless telemetry node that broadcasts nerve conduction velocity data to the attending physician's interface, allowing real-time monitoring of regeneration progress without invasive follow-up procedures. It is available in 23 standardized diameter configurations to match nerve gauges from fine digital branches to major peripheral trunks like the ulnar and sciatic.

The SX-11 occupies a peculiar market niche: it is primarily prescribed by Zheng-Dao-affiliated clinics as a prerequisite procedure before installing their higher-margin neural augmentation hardware, ensuring nerve pathways are intact and optimized for implant integration. Critics within the medical community note that this creates a financial incentive to recommend NerveBridge procedures even in cases where natural regeneration might suffice, effectively making the conduit a gatekeeping product for augmentation access.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric OsteoMatrix Flex-3 Bone Regeneration Scaffold#

The OsteoMatrix Flex-3 is a bioelectric bone regeneration scaffold system consisting of a patient-customized porous titanium-ceramic lattice printed to match the geometry of the damaged skeletal region, embedded with Zheng-Dao's proprietary piezoelectric microfilaments. These filaments generate micro-electrical fields in response to mechanical loading — mimicking the natural bioelectric signals that govern osteoblast activity — and accelerate bone ingrowth into the scaffold structure at rates 3.2x faster than passive scaffold competitors. The Flex-3 designation refers to the third-generation flexible integration zones at the scaffold's margins, which use a graduated porosity gradient to prevent the stress-shielding fractures that plagued rigid-margin earlier models. The scaffold is designed to be fully resorbed by host bone tissue over 18-24 months, leaving no permanent implant material.

The manufacturing process requires a pre-procedure CT scan fed into Zheng-Dao's cloud fabrication system, which produces the customized scaffold within 6 hours using sintered ceramic-titanium powder beds. This tight turnaround has made the OsteoMatrix system viable for trauma applications, not just elective reconstructive surgery. The embedded piezoelectric network also serves a secondary diagnostic function: an external wand reader (the ZD OsteoScan RS-2) can interrogate the scaffold's electrical output pattern to assess bone ingrowth progress non-invasively, replacing the need for follow-up imaging in most cases.

The OsteoMatrix Flex-3 has found a significant secondary market in GLMZ's augmentation-adjacent economy. Citizens who require skeletal reinforcement to support heavy cybernetic limb attachments — where the bone-implant interface is a chronic failure point — use the Flex-3 scaffold to pre-strengthen attachment sites before augmentation surgery. Zheng-Dao markets this application through licensed augmentation clinics but quietly ignores its use in unlicensed chop-shop pre-augmentation prep.

  • A labor organizer in the Palladian Construction workforce has compiled records showing that the company's medical contractors systematically omit OsteoMatrix scaffolding from worker augmentation packages despite internal safety assessments recommending it — she needs someone to get those internal documents out before the next contract renewal
  • A counterfeiting ring has been producing OsteoMatrix Flex-3 scaffolds using incorrect piezoelectric filament specifications — the scaffolds look identical but generate fields that inhibit rather than promote bone growth, and the first wave of patients is beginning to present with catastrophic scaffold failures
  • Zheng-Dao's cloud fabrication system for the OsteoMatrix has been compromised — someone has been inserting microscopic structural weaknesses into scaffolds destined for specific patients, and the modifications are subtle enough that they won't manifest as failure for 18 months

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric PulseGuard CR-2 Cardiac Rhythm Stabilization Implant#

The PulseGuard CR-2 is a subdermal cardiac rhythm management implant roughly the size of a large coin, seated beneath the left clavicle via a 15-minute outpatient procedure. It combines a next-generation adaptive pacemaker with a bioelectric defibrillation module capable of delivering a precisely calibrated shock to terminate ventricular fibrillation without the energy demands that made earlier implanted defibrillators bulky and short-lived. The CR-2 harvests a portion of its operating power from the body's own bioelectric gradient using Zheng-Dao's established microcurrent harvesting architecture, supplemented by a solid-state reserve cell with a projected 12-year lifespan under normal load.

What distinguishes the CR-2 from legacy cardiac implants is its real-time arrhythmia classification engine — a compact neuromorphic processing unit that continuously analyzes cardiac waveforms and distinguishes between benign rhythm variations (common in heavily augmented individuals whose implants introduce bioelectric interference) and genuinely dangerous arrhythmias requiring intervention. This dramatically reduces inappropriate shock delivery, which had been a leading cause of augmentation-related cardiac injury in GLMZ's densely wired population. The device communicates with Saltmarsh Telecom's health monitoring infrastructure when in range, forwarding anonymized rhythm data to Zheng-Dao's cardiac analytics network.

The CR-2 is standard issue for any citizen receiving thoracic augmentation above a certain implant density threshold, and Tier 1 corporate employees frequently receive it as a proactive measure regardless of cardiac history. In lower tiers, access is more complicated — the device is theoretically available through subsidized Tier 3 health programs, but waiting lists run 18 months or longer, and counterfeit units using inferior capacitor arrays have caused several documented deaths by delayed defibrillation. A persistent rumor in security circles holds that the CR-2's Saltmarsh data uplink can be exploited to deliver a targeted cardiac event — a claim Zheng-Dao dismisses as technically impossible and Arcturus Defense Solutions has reportedly been investigating for three years.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric SynapseWeave NX-6 Cortical Mesh Implant#

The SynapseWeave NX-6 is a ultra-thin biocompatible neural mesh — roughly 40 microns thick — that is injected in a folded suspension state and self-deploys across the cortical surface over 72 hours, guided by Zheng-Dao's proprietary electrotrophic migration algorithm. Once seated, the mesh's 2.4 million electrode nodes interface with native cortical tissue, creating a dense bidirectional communication layer between organic neurons and external digital systems. Unlike earlier invasive drill-point implants, the NX-6 achieves full-surface coverage without cranial surgery, instead entering via a lumbar spinal injection and traveling the cerebrospinal fluid pathways to the brain. The NX-6 distinguishes itself from competitors through its adaptive impedance matching — the mesh continuously recalibrates each electrode node to compensate for glial scarring and neural plasticity changes, maintaining signal fidelity over years rather than degrading. It supports simultaneous sensory augmentation, memory indexing, and direct device control. The mesh also includes a passive bioelectric harvesting layer that siphons enough energy from neural firing patterns to maintain low-power operations without a dedicated battery. Primary users are Tier 2 and above corporate knowledge workers, Saltmarsh Telecom's licensed netrunner corps, and the wealthier end of the grey-market augmentation scene.
